v1-onboarding.title: A card with a Google button
v1-onboarding.why: The first self-serve flow: sign in, pilot terms, your product, your demo, then the pilot home.
v1-onboarding.ask: screen-by-screen onboarding (login, T&C), ending on a bare-minimum pilot dashboard with a fun delightful animation

v1-onboarding.title: Pilot terms on screen
v1-onboarding.why: Step two asked people to agree to pilot terms; later cut, since every question on screen is a reason to stop.

v1-onboarding.title: “What do you sell?”
v1-onboarding.why: Step three collected a website and what you sell up front, before the demo was made.

v1-onboarding.title: Waiting with the log at sea
v1-onboarding.why: The pilot home showed the duck on its log sailing toward the island as the progress bar, with time left.

v1-onboarding.title: A progress bar on every step
v1-onboarding.why: A five-segment bar beside “Step N of 5”, because people stay in a flow when they can see how much is left.
v1-onboarding.ask: Is there a progress bar to show people where they are in the onboarding process?

v1-onboarding.title: A three.js helm, four logos
v1-onboarding.why: A hero moment before sign-in: the helm’s spokes fold into the hub, and four sign-in logos land on the rim.
v1-onboarding.ask: Don't start with step two, it feels weird.

v1-onboarding.title: The problem question
v1-onboarding.why: A demo is built around a problem, so the question now asks what problem the product solves.
v1-onboarding.ask: Is there a better way to ask 'What do you sell?'

v1-onboarding.title: Google only, the hub as button
v1-onboarding.why: One choice means no decision; after the spokes fold in, the hub itself becomes the one thing to press.
v1-onboarding.ask: The only sign-in option we want is Google, so reimagine the animation.

v1-storyboard.title: One mic for the whole demo
v1-storyboard.why: The first storyboard: watch the demo, review each shot, and a “Talk through changes” mic for spoken feedback.
v1-storyboard.ask: Speaking feedback instead of clicking around.

v1-storyboard.title: An A/B ask in a dialog
v1-storyboard.why: An A/B button opened a lightbox to describe two versions to test, with Generate at the bottom.
v1-storyboard.ask: an A/B button that opens a lightbox, and Generate at the bottom.

v1-storyboard.title: Watch, then review; shots reorder
v1-storyboard.why: Two numbered sections for the page’s two jobs; Approve, Change and Cut sit in the same place on every card.
v1-storyboard.ask: Critique the storyboard from an experienced product designer perspective. I feel like there's not real visual hierarchy.

v1-storyboard.title: Shots as sheets; approved stands apart
v1-storyboard.why: Each shot became a white sheet on a faint off-white ground, and an approved sheet takes a green glow.
v1-storyboard.ask: The UI on the storyboard edit page looks like clip art. Can you make it look more premium? The shading looks so cheap.

v1-storyboard.title: Storyboards waited in a list
v1-storyboard.why: Before my edits: a storyboard sat under Demos until someone pressed Review.

v1-storyboard.title: Are you sure, before a cut
v1-storyboard.why: Generate can’t be taken back, so one question at the point of no return prevents a lost shot.
v1-storyboard.ask: For cut, have are you sure you want to cut these, you can't undo this action.

v1-storyboard.title: Publish on the title row
v1-storyboard.why: Publish moved onto the title row after the legend, and Say changes moved beside the video.
v1-storyboard.ask: does the storyboard editor make sense? is there anything redundant there?

v1-storyboard.title: Calmer decisions on every shot
v1-storyboard.why: Approve, Change and Cut became a raised white thumb; approved shows a tide wash and a tick, within the palette.
v1-storyboard.ask: I really really hate the way the editor look when you press approve change and cut

v1-storyboard.title: The first storyboard: one mic for the whole demo
v1-storyboard.why: Before my edits: the first build of the storyboard.

v1-storyboard.title: One shot open: Says and On screen, a mic each
Hover a shot to pick it up
Read the note before it applies
Applied, and the shot marked Edited
A cut leaves Undo in its place

connect.title: Sending accounts, inside Settings
connect.why: Before my edits: LinkedIn and email were connected from a Settings tab.

connect.title: Account cards borrowed from Settings
connect.why: Product questions moved to the kickoff call; connecting LinkedIn and X joined onboarding, reusing the sending-accounts card.
connect.ask: The questions will be triaged on a call. All we need is login, face cloning and demo creation.

connect.title: Lines run from the helm
connect.why: The step became a centred column, with signal lines from the helm to each account so the connection is visible.
connect.ask: Step three still looks wrong. The lines used to logo was better positioned.

connect.title: A sidebar of sections
connect.why: Onboarding gained a TurboTax-style sidebar; a section turns bold only once an account is really connected.
connect.ask: I want a side bar during the onboarding flow that bolds the sections that are completed, like TurboTax

connect.title: Centred cards, docked buttons
connect.why: Each card’s logo, name, line and button now stack on the card’s centre, and the repeated heading row came out.
connect.ask: all the stuff in section two of onboarding isnt perfectly centered. make sure you check every group of items is centered.

connect.title: One compact panel
connect.why: The helm’s lines land on one white panel of two rows: half the height, and the diagram is the control.
connect.ask: connect to linkedin feels too spacious- reimagine this

connect.title: Back to two cards
connect.why: The compact panel was reverted to the helm, its dotted lines and two centred cards, the shape she knew and trusted.
connect.ask: make the linkedin conect page what it used to be. this is really weird now.

connect.title: Two buttons under the helm
connect.why: A box around a lone button felt bland, and the diagram already shows the logos, so two buttons remain.
connect.ask: connect to linkedin and connect to x feels too bland in their box now. maybe just have the connect linkedin, connect x buttions?

connect.title: A quiet Disconnect
connect.why: Once connected, only an outlined Disconnect remains; the diagram’s tick says connected, and Undo holds its place for five seconds.
connect.ask: when you connect, the way disconnect looks is odd. maybe we dont need all that disconect info. reimagine disconnect.

leads.title: The old Audiences page
leads.why: Before my edits: lists, contacts and companies in three tabs.

leads.title: Drop a CSV, or say names
leads.why: A new step after Connect: the demo is for leads, so naming them right after the sending accounts reads in order.
leads.ask: …upload a sheet like a cvs to upload their lead list.. they should also be able to upload it with voice

leads.title: Leads appear as you speak
leads.why: Each spoken lead lands as a row you can see and remove, so a mishearing costs one ×.

leads.title: Upload only in onboarding
leads.why: Onboarding stays one simple action; describing who you want is a strategy decision, so voice moved to the dashboard.
leads.ask: the voice thing for the lead list shouldn't be in onboarding.

leads.title: Excel too; the sheet uploads
leads.why: People upload whatever they already have, so .xlsx joined CSV, and the sheet itself became the upload.
leads.ask: can we upload stuff more than a csv, also we can drop the upload csv button on the top

leads.title: The drop zone fills the sheet
leads.why: A 74px gap left over from a removed header came out, so the drop zone fills the sheet.
leads.ask: why is there so much space above drop your lead list here?

leads.title: Four steps, Undo per upload
leads.why: Where it landed: onboarding is four steps, and each upload keeps its own Undo under the sheet.

team.title: Team, inside Settings
team.why: Before my edits: members and invites in a Settings tab.

team.title: Members, roles and auto-join
team.why: Invite your team arrived as the workspace’s own Team panel, with Make my pilot demo at its foot.

team.title: “All hands on deck” crew wheel
team.why: A helm with a handle per teammate; a new invite flies its handle in, throws sparks and spins the wheel.
team.ask: Invite your team can feel more fun and visually dramatic — generate excitement with Three.js and fun CSS.

team.title: A lit 3D helm
team.why: The crew wheel became a lit 3D helm on a deep-tide stage, spinning a full turn per invite.
team.ask: The all hands on deck idea doesn't feel bold and premium.

team.title: A flat row of discs
team.why: The 3D wheel felt hyper-real; a calm flat row lets each new person settling in be the one moment of delight.
team.ask: Too hyper realistic on the all hands thing and I think you need to drop the wheel. The concept isn't premium.

team.title: Invite your team, plainly worded
team.why: The theme lives in the visuals; the words name the real value, working together.
team.ask: I don't like the words on deck on that page.

team.title: Invites as chips, free to remove
team.why: Type and press Enter or paste a To: line; each address becomes a chip with an ×, sent only on Create demo.
team.ask: I should always be able to undo an action I just did.

team.title: A + leads the row
team.why: You already know you’re on the team; a + invites action, and the row fills as you add people.
team.ask: Drop MA, make it a plus sign.

team.title: Paste a list, then Start pilot
team.why: Where it landed: the last step’s button is Start pilot, which sends the invites and leads and starts the pilot.

face.title: The old Face cloning page
face.why: Before my edits: the script beside a small camera, and a permission box.

face.title: Two boxes to tick
face.why: A face and voice step joined onboarding: tick good light and clean audio, then the recorder opens in the card.
face.ask: Face cloning needs to be part of this, and if they opt out it needs to be the first step on the dashboard.

face.title: A live camera check
face.why: People tick boxes without checking, so the camera now measures light and quiet before a take is recorded.
face.ask: Face cloning should have a camera-on moment that automatically checks for the things it asks for.

face.title: One centred porthole
face.why: The step became one centred porthole; light and quiet fill as gauges on its rim, and the bolts light up when ready.
face.ask: Reimagine step 3. It's not fun enough, feels unbalanced and disjointed.

face.title: One ring: light, then quiet
face.why: One check at a time, like fingerprint setup; the two gauges are halves of one ring, with no box around them.

face.title: Read words turn dark
face.why: Black on blue hid your progress, so words to read are grey, read words go dark, and a caret marks your place.

face.title: Out of onboarding, into the menu
face.why: Clients can’t film while on a call, so face cloning left onboarding; the menu keeps Face & Voice until it’s recorded.
face.ask: I feel like we removed too much from the side bar. it should have, face cloning (until its completed)

face.title: The one dark card on Home
face.why: In a test with 8 people, 6 preferred an alert at the top of the dashboard over a pop-up by the tab.
face.ask: design a widget that goes above pipeline face cloning make it stand out.

face.title: The same card, by email
face.why: The email after onboarding uses the same card; its video is a still that opens the dashboard, where the welcome plays.
face.ask: the goal is after onboarding we email them with a face cloning button/link for them to be routed. design this email as well.

face.title: The old Face cloning page
face.why: Before my edits: the script beside a small camera, and a permission box.

face.title: Full screen, room and all
face.why: In the small porthole the light on a face couldn't be judged. Full screen, the check reads the skin in the oval against the room behind it, and a light bar shows where you stand.
face.ask: the reason that you were not able to pick up that camera lighting is because when the viewport is small and not full screen, it doesn't ... evaluate the lighting properly

face.title: The take, on the Face & Voice page
face.why: The script sits above the camera, so you read each line and see yourself at once. The camera stays on from the check.
face.ask: when they do the lighting check I need this full screen. but when they record I do the smaller view port that I created.

face.title: Paused, the take kept
face.why: Pause keeps the take. Leaving the tab pauses it too, and Resume picks up at the same sentence.
face.ask: what is built in for people who get interrupted when they start recording?

face.title: Saved, your voice on its way
face.why: The take saves and your voice is prepared in the background, so you can leave the page.

dashboard.title: The old Home, under a 12-item menu
dashboard.why: Before my edits: every page of the first dashboard sat in one long menu, with tabs inside tabs.

dashboard.title: A left menu, three sections
dashboard.why: Home answers three questions in order: Check-in for how sending goes, Strategy for who gets it, Demo styles for what works.
dashboard.ask: When they publish, we go to the main dashboard: a menu on the left…

dashboard.title: The old Home: an Overview page
dashboard.why: Before my edits: an Overview of sending, results and meetings in small tables.

dashboard.title: One section per screen
dashboard.why: Each section is a screen tall and snaps, so widgets can be big, each with its own shape.
dashboard.ask: I think things should feel big and sizable. like to the point where only one section is visible at a time as you scroll.

dashboard.title: The old Metrics page
dashboard.why: Before my edits: numbers by channel in a table.

dashboard.title: Running totals, faces for meetings
dashboard.why: Every Check-in widget became a graph over time as a running total, and meetings show one face per meeting.
dashboard.ask: I want this dashboard to be premium and organized. this doesn't feel clean at all

dashboard.title: Every old page in the menu
dashboard.why: Everything from the deployed dashboard joined the menu so customers lost no page: twelve items, with tabs inside tabs.
dashboard.ask: I need to make sure that all the stuff that is currently in the currently deployed dashbaord is featured on this website somewhere

dashboard.title: Three menu items, account behind you
dashboard.why: Each menu item answers one question, deeper pages open from the widget they deepen, and set-up sits behind your name.
dashboard.ask: less is more with this nav bar … right now this is overwhleming.

dashboard.title: Each week on its own
dashboard.why: A rising total hides a bad week, so charts show each week, and only the pointed-at number turns blue.
dashboard.ask: also we dont want cumulutive graphs.

dashboard.title: Actions first: Approvals in the menu
dashboard.why: Approvals waits on you and was buried, so the menu grew to Home, Approvals, Inbox, Check-in, Strategy, Demos and Face & Voice.
dashboard.ask: I feel like we removed too much from the side bar … approvals is an action thing that needs to be more readily visible.

dashboard.title: Look B: Pipeline on blue
dashboard.why: A white menu column frames the work, white widgets stand out on a blue page, and every axis carries labels.
dashboard.ask: include more labels in the graphs, can you make the bigger number even bigger lets go with look b

launch.title: Results and an A/B test
launch.why: The pilot dashboard grew Results and an A/B test, since a pilot is judged on whether demos earn replies.
launch.ask: I think there are more elements to the dashboard, like adding a new demo, A/B testing, what the results of that look like.

launch.title: One big demo, Edit and Publish
launch.why: Before anything is published there is one job, picking the demo, so results and the A/B test came off.
launch.ask: The pilot dashboard will only have one thing: an enlarged preview of the demo video with an edit button to the right

launch.title: A message in a bottle
launch.why: Sending the first demo is the pilot’s big moment; the demo rolls into a bottle that splashes down, then “Sent”.
launch.ask: The demo is rolled up and dropped into a message bottle that comes up from under, and then the message in a bottle plops/splashes down.

launch.title: A centred, cinematic demo
launch.why: The demo is the hero, framed by Publish and Edit, and the picked version sits in a pressed-in well.
launch.ask: The big demo is centered. It's cinematic and premium and dramatic, edit on the right of the demo, publish on the left.

launch.title: The launch in three.js
launch.why: Fireworks became rockets with ember trails, the card real paper, and a glass bottle rises out of a moonlit sea.
launch.ask: The rolling up looks wrong. And the plop looks wrong. Can you use Flora and three.js. Also the fireworks could look better.

launch.title: The launch in ASCII
launch.why: Redrawn in the sea’s ASCII, so it speaks the same language as every other sea in the product.
launch.ask: remake the toast animation with ascii characters.

launch.title: The demo flies into the menu
launch.why: The flight runs as one smooth three.js motion with real tilt and shadow, settling into Demos as the dashboard fades in.
launch.ask: the way the demo after the celebration moves to the nav bar is choppy and not smooth

launch.title: “Sent!” on an even night
launch.why: The night fades up evenly in 900ms with the card, so the moment never snaps to sudden dark.
launch.ask: removes the drip effect from the blue

email.title: Set up, on its own
email.why: 2 people opened the email and left it.

email.title: Set up, or Remind me tomorrow
email.why: Remind me tomorrow brings it back to the top of their inbox at a better time.
